t: You're looking at the National Submariners' War Memorial on the Victoria Embankment, between Waterloo Bridge and Blackfriars Bridge. It remembers Royal Navy submariners who died in the First and Second World Wars. In the First World War alone, the service grew from 57 vessels to 137, lost 54 submarines, and over 1,300 submariners were killed. The sculptor was Frederick Brook Hitch, son of the architectural sculptor Nathaniel Hitch. It's Grade II* listed, and each year, on the Sunday before Remembrance Sunday, submariners walk here and lay wreaths.
